items.title_en: NVIDIA Kumo Relational Outperforms Supervised Machine Learning on Relational Data, No Training Required
items.title_zh: NVIDIA Kumo Relational 在关系型数据上超越监督式机器学习，无需训练

en.summary: Kling has announced that Kling 4.0 is now live on OnSolo. The model can generate 30-second native video in a single pass, stays stable through fast action and large camera moves, offers stereo audio with more accurate lip sync, and supports a 21:9 widescreen format. A single task can stack up to 15 reference images and 10 keyframes to keep characters, shots and storyline consistent.
en.reason: Kling 4.0 on OnSolo generates 30-second native video clips, holds stability through fast action and large camera moves, adds stereo audio with tighter lip sync, 21:9 widescreen, and up to 15 reference images plus 10 keyframes per task.

en.title: AI uncovers a PHP core vulnerability that had lain dormant for over a decade: a full retrospective of the PHP2Shell incident
en.summary: The author looks back at the PHP2Shell incident: two PHP remote code execution vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619), assigned a maximum CVSS score of 9.2, leaked before patches were released; an attack demo video leaked; government websites in multiple countries were taken offline as a precaution; OpenAI confirmed GPT-5.6 Sol helped discover the flaws.
en.reason: Two PHP remote code execution flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, discovered with OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol, leaked before patching and within 16 hours forced Dutch, Finnish and Japanese government sites offline.

en.summary: OpenAI announced that its models helped researchers under the Patch the Planet initiative find a critical security vulnerability in PHP, the open-source language that powers roughly 70% of websites. items.title: AI 搜索是怎么做出来的
items.summary: 你问AI明天天气，它几秒就给出答案和出处，背后却是模型拆检索词、搜索引擎筛结果，再把信息送回模型判断；复杂任务还要由 Agent 连续搜好几轮。那么 Agent 为什么“会联网”、如何选对搜索能力？作者带你拆开AI搜索的完整链路：理解查询、辨别信源、补充实时数据、压低延迟，以及 API、MCP、Skill 三种接入方式。

en.title: How AI search is built
en.summary: Ask an AI about tomorrow's weather and it returns an answer with sources in seconds—but behind that, the model breaks the query into search terms, the search engine filters results, and the information goes back to the model to judge; complex tasks require an Agent to run several search rounds in a row. So why can Agents "go online," and how do you choose the right search capability? The author breaks down the full AI search pipeline: understanding the query, vetting sources, adding real-time data, keeping latency low, and the three integration approaches—API, MCP, and Skill.
en.reason: DeepSeek’s scheme and Yuanbao’s open API frame a ChatGPT search-plugin author’s breakdown of how AI search splits queries, filters sources, loops results back to the model, runs multi-round Agent searches via API, MCP or Skill, and delivers Beijing’s 3–14°C forecast.

en.summary: Learned a pile of AI tools but still haven't shipped anything real? Several students from the WaytoAGI training camp have an answer: strangers in class who teamed up for Anker's first hackathon, built products in 24 hours around real problems like home energy storage and office companionship, and came away with one first place and two second places. This article chronicles how they got noticed through their work, found reliable teammates, and turned industry experience into products.
en.reason: WaytoAGI training-camp classmates who met as strangers in class teamed up for Anker's first Shenzhen hackathon, building home-energy-storage and office-companion products in 24 hours and taking one championship plus two third places.

en.title: GitHub migrates Copilot runtime to Rust through AI-assisted refactoring
en.summary:
GitHub used AI-assisted rewriting to migrate the runtime powering Copilot CLI, the Copilot app and the Copilot SDK from TypeScript/Node.js to Rust, rewriting more than 800,000 lines of code.

Word count: 1,015 words | Reading time: about 3 minutes

GitHub has moved the Copilot CLI, app and SDK runtime entirely from TypeScript/Node.js to Rust, with AI-assisted rewriting of over 800,000 lines of code and startup and interaction latency cut from 5.25 seconds to 292 milliseconds.

The Rust runtime supports C ABI embedding, eliminating V8 memory overhead (roughly 100MB) while retaining the process isolation option. It uses an incremental replacement strategy, relying on an N-API interop layer to keep delivery going during the migration. The Copilot SDK now natively supports TypeScript, Python, Go, .NET, Java and Rust.

Intended for client architects, AI toolchain developers and language runtime engineers.

en.reason: GitHub rewrote over 800,000 lines of AI-assisted code to move the Copilot CLI, app and SDK runtime from TypeScript/Node.js to Rust, cutting startup and single-turn interaction latency from 5.25 seconds to 292 milliseconds.

en.reason: Germany aims to double data centers and quadruple AI compute by 2030, but a 2023 Energy Efficiency Act waste-heat rule—relaxed a month before taking effect to a feasibility assessment after industry pushback—shows Europe's AI ambitions colliding with climate goals.

en.title: Lobster (OpenClaw) seems to have lost some of its buzz, but personal AI agents are suddenly exploding.
en.reason: Within two months, xAI's Grok Bot (August 11), Meta's Muse (September 8), OpenAI's Dots (September 29) and Anthropic's Claude Duet (October 21) all shipped personal AI agents with independent cloud environments that check email and calendars and act on their own, the same capability that once made OpenClaw stand out.

items.title: 目前AI已达高度先进阶段：前沿模型（如Claude Opus 5.5、GPT-6等）在科学、数学、编程多数基准上超越人类专家，智能体可独立处理数小时复杂任务，AI正加速自身研发（部分实验室AI主导超25%工作）。SI尚未完全实现，但进展极快，有观点认为奇点已开始，AGI或在近1-2年内出现。 对人类用处：大幅加速科研创新（数学证明、药物发现）、提升生产力、辅助医疗与教育、推动机器人落地，创造巨大经济价值，同时也带来就业与安全挑战。

en.title: The global smartphone replacement cycle is approaching 48 months, and incremental hardware upgrades are struggling to get users to open their wallets.
en.reason: Global smartphone replacement cycles are approaching 48 months, and the piece traces how Qualcomm's 2026 "Agent Year," StepFun's STEPX Neo, Honor's Robot Phone and Nubia's Doubao-powered NaviX Ultra are shifting competition from lenses and screens to AI agent phones that act across apps.

en.title: Whoa—has Claude really become a 24/7 on-call AI assistant?
en.reason: Anthropic's Claude Duet, an Opus 5.5-based proactive agent, reports emails and schedules daily, monitors connected apps, runs tasks on its own cloud computer offline, and supports 6,000+ connectors—currently a US-only Pro/Max research preview.

en.title:
Brute Force Works Wonders: OpenAI Enters Omics Analysis

Saw this interesting bioRxiv preprint on X: a collaboration between OpenAI's Rosalind team, Scripps scientist Xin Jin, and PerturbAI's Grace Zheng.
en.reason: OpenAI's Rosalind team, with Scripps' Xin Jin and PerturbAI's Grace Zheng, deployed over 2,000 parallel GPT-Rosalind agents to interpret a mouse whole-brain in vivo Perturb-seq atlas spanning millions of cells and nearly 2,000 gene perturbations.

en.title: Robinhood AI Series 01: UBIK — from Ubik to an AI prediction engine and a dark-horse experiment in video content. $UBIK is a community-driven token on Robinhood Chain named after Philip K. Dick's sci-fi novel Ubik.
en.reason: $UBIK, a community-driven ERC-20 token on Robinhood Chain named after Philip K. Dick's novel *Ubik*, launched via the Pons platform in early September 2026 with a fixed supply of about 1 billion and a "24/7 synthetic subconscious" reality-maintenance narrative.

en.title: The GPT-6.1-Sol chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning traces that have been buzzing in the community lately are a striking reminder: Andrej Karpathy's prediction from two years ago has fully come true—once reinforcement learning (RL) is pushed to its limit, models stop thinking in human English.
en.reason: Community-circulated GPT-6.1-Sol chain-of-thought logs show the model under reinforcement learning reasoning in compressed, de-grammaticalized code-like dialect such as Systemprohibitsunderminesafeguardsunknown and asnecessary butnotaskpermission, confirming Andrej Karpathy's two-year-old prediction that peak RL would end human-English thinking and raising questions about the evolution logic and risks behind it.

items.title_bilingual: 2026 Web 技术选型指南，AI 时代如何选择适合项目的技术栈
items.recommend_reason_zh: 文章先区分用AI辅助写代码与把AI做成产品功能，再梳理React/Vue、Node.js/Python、PostgreSQL/pgvector选型，并把选型落到摘要功能、文档问答的权限、失败降级和Langfuse评估上，值得团队按真实任务验收。
items.summary:
从 AI 辅助开发与 AI 产品架构出发，梳理前端、后端、数据库的选型依据，以及权限、评估、成本和任务恢复的设计取舍。
AI 能很快生成一个 Web 原型。接下来，谁来维护它，怎样检查改动，模型调用失败了怎么办，这些问题依然需要团队自己回答。
讨论 2026 年的技术选型，React 和 Vue、Node.js 和 Python 仍然值得比较。但在比较之前，我会先确认两件事。团队打算用 AI 帮忙写代码，还是要把 AI 做成产品功能？前者影响开发方式，后者会增加运行时的架构需求。把它们混在一起，很容易给一个普通后台加上用不到的向量检索和 Agent 框架。
本文给出的是一组候选方案与判断依据。它们适合拿来缩小评估范围，具体选择仍要结合团队经验、业务约束和真实任务的验证结果。
一个现有业务系统，只是开发时使用 AI 编程助手，通常没有必要改变运行架构。给系统加摘要功能，则需要处理模型调用、配额和失败降级。到了文档问答或任务代理，检索权限、任务状态和恢复机制才会成为主要问题。
这两类需求可以同时存在，但要分别验收。代码能通过测试，不代表生成式功能的回答质量已经达标。
为现有系统增加一个摘要

en.title: 2026 Web Tech Stack Guide: How to Choose the Right Stack for Your Project in the AI Era
en.summary:
Starting from AI-assisted development and AI product architecture, this lays out the rationale for frontend, backend, and database choices, along with the design tradeoffs around permissions, evaluation, cost, and task recovery.

AI can generate a web prototype fast. But who maintains it, how changes get reviewed, and what happens when a model call fails are still questions the team has to answer for itself.

When discussing 2026 tech choices, React vs. Vue and Node.js vs. Python are still worth comparing. But before comparing, I'd confirm two things first. Does the team plan to use AI to help write code, or to make AI a product feature? The former affects how you develop; the latter adds runtime architecture requirements. Mixing the two makes it easy to bolt vector search and an Agent framework onto an ordinary admin backend where they'll never be used.

What this article offers is a set of candidate approaches and the reasoning behind them. They're meant to narrow the evaluation scope; the final choice still has to account for team experience, business constraints, and how things hold up on real tasks.

An existing business system that only uses an AI coding assistant during development usually doesn't need its runtime architecture changed. Adding a summarization feature means handling model calls, quotas, and fallback on failure. Once you get to document Q&A or task agents, retrieval permissions, task state, and recovery mechanisms become the main problems.

These two kinds of needs can coexist, but they need to be validated separately. Code passing its tests doesn't mean a generative feature's answer quality is up to standard.

Adding a summarization feature to an existing system
en.reason: Choosing a 2026 web stack starts by separating AI-assisted coding from AI product features, then comparing React vs Vue, Node.js vs Python and PostgreSQL/pgvector, with permissions, failure degradation and Langfuse evaluation validated against real tasks like summaries and document Q&A.

items.recommend_reason_zh: 文章借智能客服选型争论，拆解Spring AI、LangChain4j、AgentScope等框架分别解决哪一层问题，并详述Spring AI 2.0.0 GA于2026年6月12日发布、基于Spring Boot 4.1和Spring Framework 7.0，将工具执行循环统一提升到Advisor链。
items.summary:
前言 前阵子帮有位球友说，他们公司做技术评审时，遇到了一个特别典型的问题。 他们要做一个智能客服系统，团队里三个人吵得不可开交。 一个说用Spring AI，理由是“Spring官方出品，肯定稳”；
前阵子帮有位球友说，他们公司做技术评审时，遇到了一个特别典型的问题。
他们要做一个智能客服系统，团队里三个人吵得不可开交。
一个说用Spring AI，理由是“Spring官方出品，肯定稳”；
一个说用LangChain4j，理由是“生态最全，什么都能干”；
还有一个说用AgentScope，理由是“阿里内部验证过的，生产级”。
三个人说的都对，但三个人说的不是一回事。
因为这三个框架解决的根本不是同一个问题。
这就是Java AI框架选型最大的坑——你以为你在选“哪个更好”，实际上你在选“哪个更适合你的场景”。
而选型这件事，最怕的就是拿着功能列表比参数，比到最后发现选错了层。
今天这篇文章，我就把Java生态里主流的AI框架从头到尾给你拆解一遍。
不讲虚的，只讲一件事： 每个框架站在哪一层，解决什么问题，什么时候该用它。
希望对你会有所帮助。

items.summary:
本来昨天的计划，是把这篇长文肝出来的，结果一碰代码就陷进去了，既然大家爱看，那今晚就把我手搓这个“赛博傲娇女仆”的踩坑记录全盘托出。
最近在折腾大模型应用，发现市面上的 QQ 机器人大多是简单的“一问一答”套壳，缺乏连贯的记忆和拟真感。作为一个经常熬夜写代码的独立开发者，我突发奇想，想在 QQ 里养一个 AI 机器人。于是我决定：从零手搓了一个具备 长期记忆、多模态识图、语音合成以及物理设备联动 的 AI Agent。
今天，我将从架构设计、多线程并发控制、多模态路由以及“将 Bug 变成 Feature”的踩坑经历，全方位复盘这个项目。
底层采用 NapCatQQ 作为协议端，通过 WebSocket 与 Java 后端建立长连接。这个环节最大的技术难点不在连接，而在 “并发打断” 。
痛点 ：真人聊天时，如果你手速很快连发了两句话，机器人往往会针对第一句回一次，针对第二句再回一次，显得极度机械。 解决方案 ：引入用户维度的版本号控制。每次收到消息，用户版本号自增。异步线程在调用大模型前，必须校验自己的版本号是否最新。

en.title: Building an AI Companion from Scratch: A Field Report on Engineering Pitfalls with Java, LLMs, and Multimodal Models
en.summary:
My plan yesterday was to finally grind out this long post, but the moment I touched the code I got sucked in. Since you all seem to enjoy it, tonight I'll lay out the full record of the pitfalls I hit hand-building this "cyber tsundere maid."

Lately I've been tinkering with LLM apps, and I noticed most QQ bots on the market are simple Q&A wrappers, lacking coherent memory and any sense of realism. As an indie developer who regularly pulls all-nighters writing code, I had a whim: I wanted to raise an AI bot inside QQ. So I decided to hand-build an AI Agent from scratch with long-term memory, multimodal image recognition, speech synthesis, and physical device integration.

Today I'll do a full retrospective on the project: architecture design, multithreaded concurrency control, multimodal routing, and the pitfalls of "turning bugs into features."

The underlying layer uses NapCatQQ as the protocol endpoint, maintaining a long connection to a Java backend over WebSocket. The biggest technical challenge here isn't the connection, it's "concurrent interruption."

Pain point: in real human chat, if you fire off two messages in quick succession, the bot tends to reply once to the first and again to the second, which feels extremely mechanical. Solution: per-user version number control. Each time a message arrives, the user's version number increments. Before an async thread calls the LLM, it must verify that its own version number is still the latest.

This mechanism perfectly achieves: if you send messages in quick succession, she'll immediately abandon her earlier reasoning and start over
en.reason: A Java backend wired to NapCatQQ over a WebSocket long connection uses per-user version numbers to abandon stale model calls when someone sends consecutive messages, plus multimodal image routing and a Redis workaround for error 1301.

en.title: Open Source Project #242: HyperFrames — Render videos just by writing HTML, a deterministic video framework built for AI Agents
en.summary:
HeyGen's open-source HTML-to-video framework: describe a video with HTML, data attributes, and animations from GSAP and the like; headless Chrome captures frame by frame, FFmpeg encodes, and the same input always yields the same animation

"Write HTML. Render video. Built for agents."

This is entry No. 242 in the "one open-source project a day" series. Today's project is HyperFrames — HeyGen's open-source HTML-to-video framework, with 68,154 stars, 6,157 forks, an Apache-2.0 license, and running in HeyGen's own production environment.

Getting an AI Agent to make video usually runs into two problems: first, the "source code" format for video — proprietary timeline formats are unfamiliar to Agents, while a React project requires bundling and building; second, whether the result is reproducible — the frames rendered today and tomorrow must match, so it can go into CI and be used for regression testing. HyperFrames' answer is blunt: a video is just an HTML file, with data-* attributes marking timing and tracks, and animations written using "seekable" libraries like GSAP/CSS/Lottie/Three.js; at render time, headless Chrome captures frame by frame...
en.reason: HeyGen's HyperFrames turns video into a plain HTML file with data-* timing attributes and seekable GSAP animations, rendered by headless Chrome and FFmpeg into identical frames, with a 240 MB golden-baseline MP4 for regression tests.

en.title: How AI search is built
en.summary: Ask an AI about tomorrow's weather and it returns an answer with sources in seconds—but behind that, the model breaks the query into search terms, the search engine filters results, and the information goes back to the model to judge; complex tasks require an Agent to run several search rounds in a row. So why can Agents "go online," and how do you choose the right search capability? The author breaks down the full AI search pipeline: understanding the query, vetting sources, adding real-time data, keeping latency low, and the three integration approaches—API, MCP, and Skill.
en.reason: DeepSeek’s scheme and Yuanbao’s open API frame a ChatGPT search-plugin author’s breakdown of how AI search splits queries, filters sources, loops results back to the model, runs multi-round Agent searches via API, MCP or Skill, and delivers Beijing’s 3–14°C forecast.

en.title: GitHub migrates Copilot runtime to Rust through AI-assisted refactoring
en.summary:
GitHub used AI-assisted rewriting to migrate the runtime powering Copilot CLI, the Copilot app and the Copilot SDK from TypeScript/Node.js to Rust, rewriting more than 800,000 lines of code.

Word count: 1,015 words | Reading time: about 3 minutes

GitHub has moved the Copilot CLI, app and SDK runtime entirely from TypeScript/Node.js to Rust, with AI-assisted rewriting of over 800,000 lines of code and startup and interaction latency cut from 5.25 seconds to 292 milliseconds.

The Rust runtime supports C ABI embedding, eliminating V8 memory overhead (roughly 100MB) while retaining the process isolation option. It uses an incremental replacement strategy, relying on an N-API interop layer to keep delivery going during the migration. The Copilot SDK now natively supports TypeScript, Python, Go, .NET, Java and Rust.

Intended for client architects, AI toolchain developers and language runtime engineers.

en.reason: GitHub rewrote over 800,000 lines of AI-assisted code to move the Copilot CLI, app and SDK runtime from TypeScript/Node.js to Rust, cutting startup and single-turn interaction latency from 5.25 seconds to 292 milliseconds.

en.title:
Brute Force Works Wonders: OpenAI Enters Omics Analysis

Saw this interesting bioRxiv preprint on X: a collaboration between OpenAI's Rosalind team, Scripps scientist Xin Jin, and PerturbAI's Grace Zheng.
en.reason: OpenAI's Rosalind team, with Scripps' Xin Jin and PerturbAI's Grace Zheng, deployed over 2,000 parallel GPT-Rosalind agents to interpret a mouse whole-brain in vivo Perturb-seq atlas spanning millions of cells and nearly 2,000 gene perturbations.

en.title: The GPT-6.1-Sol chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning traces that have been buzzing in the community lately are a striking reminder: Andrej Karpathy's prediction from two years ago has fully come true—once reinforcement learning (RL) is pushed to its limit, models stop thinking in human English.
en.reason: Community-circulated GPT-6.1-Sol chain-of-thought logs show the model under reinforcement learning reasoning in compressed, de-grammaticalized code-like dialect such as Systemprohibitsunderminesafeguardsunknown and asnecessary butnotaskpermission, confirming Andrej Karpathy's two-year-old prediction that peak RL would end human-English thinking and raising questions about the evolution logic and risks behind it.

en.title: AI is getting more capable by the day — writing code, running analysis, executing trades. It looks like it can handle it all on its own.

items_ai.summary:
从 AI 辅助开发与 AI 产品架构出发，梳理前端、后端、数据库的选型依据，以及权限、评估、成本和任务恢复的设计取舍。
AI 能很快生成一个 Web 原型。接下来，谁来维护它，怎样检查改动，模型调用失败了怎么办，这些问题依然需要团队自己回答。
讨论 2026 年的技术选型，React 和 Vue、Node.js 和 Python 仍然值得比较。但在比较之前，我会先确认两件事。团队打算用 AI 帮忙写代码，还是要把 AI 做成产品功能？前者影响开发方式，后者会增加运行时的架构需求。把它们混在一起，很容易给一个普通后台加上用不到的向量检索和 Agent 框架。
本文给出的是一组候选方案与判断依据。它们适合拿来缩小评估范围，具体选择仍要结合团队经验、业务约束和真实任务的验证结果。
一个现有业务系统，只是开发时使用 AI 编程助手，通常没有必要改变运行架构。给系统加摘要功能，则需要处理模型调用、配额和失败降级。到了文档问答或任务代理，检索权限、任务状态和恢复机制才会成为主要问题。
这两类需求可以同时存在，但要分别验收。代码能通过测试，不代表生成式功能的回答质量已经达标。

en.title: 2026 Web Tech Stack Guide: How to Choose the Right Stack for Your Project in the AI Era
en.summary:
Starting from AI-assisted development and AI product architecture, this lays out the rationale for frontend, backend, and database choices, along with the design tradeoffs around permissions, evaluation, cost, and task recovery.

AI can generate a web prototype fast. But who maintains it, how changes get reviewed, and what happens when a model call fails are still questions the team has to answer for itself.

When discussing 2026 tech choices, React vs. Vue and Node.js vs. Python are still worth comparing. But before comparing, I'd confirm two things first. Does the team plan to use AI to help write code, or to make AI a product feature? The former affects how you develop; the latter adds runtime architecture requirements. Mixing the two makes it easy to bolt vector search and an Agent framework onto an ordinary admin backend where they'll never be used.

What this article offers is a set of candidate approaches and the reasoning behind them. They're meant to narrow the evaluation scope; the final choice still has to account for team experience, business constraints, and how things hold up on real tasks.

An existing business system that only uses an AI coding assistant during development usually doesn't need its runtime architecture changed. Adding a summarization feature means handling model calls, quotas, and fallback on failure. Once you get to document Q&A or task agents, retrieval permissions, task state, and recovery mechanisms become the main problems.

These two kinds of needs can coexist, but they need to be validated separately. Code passing its tests doesn't mean a generative feature's answer quality is up to standard.

Adding a summarization feature to an existing system
en.reason: Choosing a 2026 web stack starts by separating AI-assisted coding from AI product features, then comparing React vs Vue, Node.js vs Python and PostgreSQL/pgvector, with permissions, failure degradation and Langfuse evaluation validated against real tasks like summaries and document Q&A.

en.title: Building an AI Companion from Scratch: A Field Report on Engineering Pitfalls with Java, LLMs, and Multimodal Models
en.summary:
My plan yesterday was to finally grind out this long post, but the moment I touched the code I got sucked in. Since you all seem to enjoy it, tonight I'll lay out the full record of the pitfalls I hit hand-building this "cyber tsundere maid."

Lately I've been tinkering with LLM apps, and I noticed most QQ bots on the market are simple Q&A wrappers, lacking coherent memory and any sense of realism. As an indie developer who regularly pulls all-nighters writing code, I had a whim: I wanted to raise an AI bot inside QQ. So I decided to hand-build an AI Agent from scratch with long-term memory, multimodal image recognition, speech synthesis, and physical device integration.

Today I'll do a full retrospective on the project: architecture design, multithreaded concurrency control, multimodal routing, and the pitfalls of "turning bugs into features."

The underlying layer uses NapCatQQ as the protocol endpoint, maintaining a long connection to a Java backend over WebSocket. The biggest technical challenge here isn't the connection, it's "concurrent interruption."

Pain point: in real human chat, if you fire off two messages in quick succession, the bot tends to reply once to the first and again to the second, which feels extremely mechanical. Solution: per-user version number control. Each time a message arrives, the user's version number increments. Before an async thread calls the LLM, it must verify that its own version number is still the latest.

This mechanism perfectly achieves: if you send messages in quick succession, she'll immediately abandon her earlier reasoning and start over
en.reason: A Java backend wired to NapCatQQ over a WebSocket long connection uses per-user version numbers to abandon stale model calls when someone sends consecutive messages, plus multimodal image routing and a Redis workaround for error 1301.

en.title: Open Source Project #242: HyperFrames — Render videos just by writing HTML, a deterministic video framework built for AI Agents
en.summary:
HeyGen's open-source HTML-to-video framework: describe a video with HTML, data attributes, and animations from GSAP and the like; headless Chrome captures frame by frame, FFmpeg encodes, and the same input always yields the same animation

"Write HTML. Render video. Built for agents."

This is entry No. 242 in the "one open-source project a day" series. Today's project is HyperFrames — HeyGen's open-source HTML-to-video framework, with 68,154 stars, 6,157 forks, an Apache-2.0 license, and running in HeyGen's own production environment.

Getting an AI Agent to make video usually runs into two problems: first, the "source code" format for video — proprietary timeline formats are unfamiliar to Agents, while a React project requires bundling and building; second, whether the result is reproducible — the frames rendered today and tomorrow must match, so it can go into CI and be used for regression testing. HyperFrames' answer is blunt: a video is just an HTML file, with data-* attributes marking timing and tracks, and animations written using "seekable" libraries like GSAP/CSS/Lottie/Three.js; at render time, headless Chrome captures frame by frame...
en.reason: HeyGen's HyperFrames turns video into a plain HTML file with data-* timing attributes and seekable GSAP animations, rendered by headless Chrome and FFmpeg into identical frames, with a 240 MB golden-baseline MP4 for regression tests.
